categories.label: Intrusive ad interruptions
categories.definition: Frequent or forced ads interrupt play so heavily that players consider quitting or uninstalling.
categories.example: 30 seconds of play.......3 minutes of ads.

categories.label: Ads misrepresent gameplay
categories.definition: Players feel the game they download does not match the gameplay that attracted them in its advertisement.
categories.example: Nothing makes me uninstall faster than booting up a game that looked fun and then it's nothing like the ad.

categories.label: Pay-to-progress pressure
categories.definition: Players reject games when meaningful progress or content feels effectively locked behind additional spending.
categories.example: If there's something in the game that is pretty much impossible to get without paying more im not going to play

categories.label: Performance and compatibility problems
categories.definition: Lag or device incompatibility disrupts or prevents smooth gameplay on mobile.

categories.label: Control and menu regressions
categories.definition: Updates can disrupt familiar control inputs and make menu navigation frustrating.
categories.example: the cursor / focus point was constantly scrolling up.

categories.label: Overbearing onboarding
categories.definition: Long tutorials and frequent prompts get in the way of players starting freely and immersing themselves in the game.
categories.example: I just want to play and figure the game out myself

categories.label: Consent-screen friction
categories.definition: Players are frustrated by having to navigate numerous privacy or consent choices before they can reach gameplay.
categories.example: have to click past more than five things just to get into the actual game
